messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: realtime-regression-detector fired for /v1/stream (service: inference-api)
ops-bot: metric: p99 latency jumped from ~320ms -> ~1.8s over last 5m (us-west-2), p95 also up. Detector id=rrd-2026-426
ops-bot: affected model: redwood-7b-v2 (variant: streaming-enabled)

jamie: ack. paging oncall. I'll join.
jamie: sasha are you oncall for infra now? can you take a look at streaming-proxy + kv-cache?

sasha: on it. investigating dashboards now — sending quick links:
- https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/inference/latency?view=streaming (shortlink)
- https://logs.redwood/query?q=service%3Astreaming-proxy%20error

sasha: quick summary from dashboards: spike at 14:02 UTC, saw increased queueing in streaming-proxy pods and a small bump in 5xx in streaming route
sasha: streaming-proxy CPU spiking on 3/6 pods, one pod showing many active connections (>1200)

miguel: checking model-side metrics (kv cache hit/miss): cache miss rate jumped from 12% -> 78% for this traffic slice around same time
miguel: looks like KV cache eviction thrash, possibly correlated with a recent config push to the cache layer (kv-cache v2.1.4 deployed ~13:58)

emily: product-ops here — any customers already bumped/paged? seeing a few support tickets for slow responses on streaming endpoints
emily: do we have % of requests affected?

jamie: preliminary: about ~2.8% of production streaming sessions show >1s tail. Error rate for stream chunking increased from 0.3% -> 1.9%
jamie: routing fallback plan in flight if infra confirms.

sasha: immediate mitigation options:
1) scale streaming-proxy up (replicas +2)
2) restart the two unhealthy streaming-proxy pods (rolling)
3) temporarily route a % of traffic to fallback model variant (redwood-7b-quant) with lower memory pressure
4) revert kv-cache config (if safe)

jamie: let's do 1 + 2 immediately. miguel, can you validate cache config rollback? if not quick, we'll do 3.

miguel: running config diff now. There was a TTL change and a slightly reduced cache size in the v2.1.4 rollout. If we restore previous cache size it needs approval from infra. I'll try a targeted restart of kv-cache pods to see if it stabilizes mem fragmentation.

sasha: scaling streaming-proxy now:
```bash
kubectl scale deploy/streaming-proxy -n inference-prod --replicas=8
``` 
sasha: also rolling restart to cycle the problematic pods:
```bash
kubectl rollout restart deploy/streaming-proxy -n inference-prod
``` 

ops-bot: action posted: restart initiated by sasha at 14:10 UTC

jamie: while that rolls, let's reduce traffic to the heavy variant. miguel — can you route 30% of streaming traffic to redwood-7b-quant? command below if infra-cli is ok:
```bash
infractl route update --service inference-api --path /v1/stream --model redwood-7b-quant --weight 30
``` 

miguel: doing that now. infractl reports config accepted.

ops-bot: routing change deployed, 30% traffic to redwood-7b-quant

sasha: pods are coming back up, CPU pressure falling on previously hot nodes. queue length dropping.

jamie: quick health check (curl against probe):
```bash
for p in $(kubectl get pods -l app=streaming-proxy -n inference-prod -o name); do kubectl exec $p -n inference-prod -- curl -sS http://localhost:8080/health || echo $p failed; done
```
jamie: all healthy after restart except streaming-proxy-3 which still has high connection backlog, we've cordoned it.

emily: customer impact: support tickets from 7 customers (rate-limited), MX score likely low for those sessions — we should mark "degraded streaming" in status page

jamie: agreed. setting status to degraded for streaming endpoints and adding note about mitigation steps.

sasha: after scale + rolling restart + routing, p99 dropped to ~360ms and p95 back to ~210ms within 6 minutes. Observed steady fall-off in 5xx for stream.

miguel: kv-cache miss rate improving to ~18% after targeted restart — suggests mem pressure + eviction was amplifying CPU on proxy

product-ops: thanks for the quick actions. can we estimate percent of total requests impacted and whether any paid customers saw errors (not just slow)?

jamie: rough numbers: 2.8% of live streaming sessions saw tail >1s, ~0.8% saw retried chunks/visible 5xx. We'll extract exact counts in the follow-up.

oncall-l: I'll take post-incident ownership. next steps:
- collect and save snapshots (grafana + logs) for 14:00-14:20 UTC
- run a full query to enumerate affected customer org_ids and surface to CS
- correlate kv-cache rollout change with timeline and verify if rollback or config size bump is safe
- schedule postmortem and assign infra + ml eng leads

oncall-l: can everyone add a brief note in the incident doc (link: https://docs.redwood/incidents/4260000001) with what they did? I'll stitch and assign follow-ups.

jamie: done. I'll paste the exact infractl commands and the kube restart logs into the doc.

sasha: flagged for follow-up: automate a detector check that correlates cache eviction rate with p99 spikes (rrd enhancement request)

miguel: will open a PR to revert the TTL/size change and run load tests against kv-cache; marking as high priority if tests reproduce.

emily: I'll inform CS and publish a short status-page update: "Partial degradation for streaming responses; mitigation in progress."

ops-bot: incident acknowledged, severity: sev3 -> monitoring for now. owners: oncall-l (incident), miguel (kv-cache), sasha (streaming-proxy).

jamie: thanks team — we're in steady state. keeping thread open for any regressions. handoff notes in incident doc, will create follow-up tickets.

sasha: closing immediate mitigation loop. please escalate if tail rises again.

oncall-l: leaving handoff: I'll monitor next 1h and schedule postmortem next week. assigning owners in tracker.

emily: adding customer impact summary to status update. thanks.

jamie: great work. :thumbsup:
